items.stem: Why is capturing design intent important in parametric CAD?

options.text: So the model updates predictably when dimensions or references change
options.rationale: Correct: good design intent makes edits propagate the way the designer expects.

options.text: So the file renders in more colours
options.rationale: Rendering colour is unrelated to design intent.

options.text: So the model uses less disk space
options.rationale: Design intent is about editability, not file size.

options.text: So the part cannot be edited at all
options.rationale: The point is controlled editability, not locking the model.

items.explanation: Correct: good design intent makes edits propagate the way the designer expects.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make a sketch robust and fully defined? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add geometric constraints such as coincident and parallel
options.rationale: Correct: constraints remove unwanted degrees of freedom.

options.text: Dimension the sketch so nothing is left under-defined
options.rationale: Correct: a fully dimensioned sketch resolves to a single geometry.
Under-defined sketches shift unpredictably on edits.
Removing references does not make a sketch robust; it often breaks it.

items.explanation: Correct: constraints remove unwanted degrees of freedom.

items.stem: An assembly fails to update after you add a mate. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The assembly is over-constrained with conflicting mates
options.rationale: Correct: conflicting mates leave the solver no valid position.
Appearance does not affect mate solving.

options.text: The drawing sheet is the wrong size
options.rationale: Sheet size is a documentation setting, not a mate constraint.

options.text: The STL export resolution is too high
options.rationale: Export settings do not drive assembly mates.

items.explanation: Correct: conflicting mates leave the solver no valid position.
